business_flow: User browses public site, accesses login/forgot-password flows, views posts and account pages. HTTP traffic contains mostly GET requests to static resources and a few form POSTs for login and password reset. No API-style numeric object IDs except post?postId=4 and my-account?id=wiener and forgot-password temp token in URL.
thought_process: Assess each of the 21 entries for the five BLV checks (IDOR BLA9, State Manipulation BLA3, Sequence Bypass BLA6, Shadow Endpoints BLA10, Internal Disclosure BLA8).
Only endpoints that exhibit a potential issue based on the available traffic will produce findings. Do not invent server behavior beyond what traffic shows.
Create one finding per vulnerable endpoint with required reproduction_guide including payload_mutation and curl_command placeholders.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Access to an apparent debug/static resource endpoint (/academyLabHeader) with no recorded successful response (response status 0 indicates possible internal or blocked endpoint or resource probing). The presence of this request suggests a shadow or lab-specific endpoint is reachable or probed. While the response status is 0 in the log, the request path looks like an undocumented lab header resource which may be a shadow endpoint.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request the /academyLabHeader path directly to probe for an undocumented/shadow endpoint.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Forgot-password POST endpoint accepts a token via query parameter (temp-forgot-password-token). If the token is client-controllable and used to set account password without additional server-side verification, client could manipulate the token to reset arbitrary accounts. The traffic shows a GET to forgot-password with temp-forgot-password-token and a subsequent POST to the same URL (entries 5 and 6), indicating the token is passed in the URL and used in the form submission flow — a potential state-manipulation risk if token validation is weak.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change the temp-forgot-password-token value in the query string to another token (e.g., replace with {{target_id}} placeholder) and POST the form to attempt password reset without valid ownership.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: my-account?id=wiener returns account page when id parameter is supplied (entry 12). Using an account identifier in a GET parameter may disclose internal usernames or allow enumeration of other users by modifying the 'id' parameter. The presence of a successful 200 response for id=wiener suggests the parameter controls which account is displayed and may leak internal user information.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change the 'id' parameter value to another username or identifier (e.g., from wiener to {{target_id}}) to attempt enumeration or view other users' account pages.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: post?postId=4 indicates object access via query parameter. If the server does not enforce authorization on post resource access, changing postId could allow access to posts the user should not see (IDOR). Entry 13 shows a GET with postId=4 returned 200, meaning post resources are addressable via predictable IDs.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'postId' from 4 to another numeric ID (e.g., {{target_id}}) to attempt access to other posts and check for authorization bypass.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Multiple requests to /resources and nested paths (entries 14-20) show probing of resource directories like /resources/labheader, /resources/labheader/js, /resources/css, etc. These appear to be automated discovery of potentially undocumented static/resource endpoints (shadow endpoints). Some entries have response status 0 indicating resources may be present but restricted; this pattern is indicative of shadow function probing.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request the listed resource paths directly to detect presence of undocumented static or lab-specific resources. No parameter changes required; just access each resource path.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: The /image endpoint (entry 7) returned response status 0 in the log which may indicate probing of a media/debug endpoint. Requesting /image could reveal debug/test images or processing endpoints not intended for public use.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Directly request the /image endpoint to see if it exposes debug or unintended image content. No body modification required.
